Internal clients can submit chargeback requests.
The system validates, deduplicates, and durably stores each accepted chargeback.
The system groups pending chargebacks into CSV batches for Mastercard.
The system sends at most 4 CSV files to Mastercard per day.
Every accepted chargeback is eventually included in a CSV and submitted.
Internal users can check the status of a chargeback and its batch.
The system supports high write throughput for incoming chargebacks.
STRONG DURABILITY - Accepted chargebacks are not lost, even during failures.
The design favors reliable eventual delivery over low latency.
Intake and submission are IDEMPOTENT so duplicates are avoided.
The system provides a full audit trail for chargebacks and batch state changes.
The system exposes clear operational visibility through logs, metrics, and alerts.
Chargeback for the dispute itself. It should hold
Batch for one CSV file sent to Mastercard.
A chargeback is when a cardholder asks their bank to reverse a card payment
because they believe something went wrong.
The bank pulls the money back from the merchant while the dispute is investigated.
The system validates and stores each chargeback durably.
The system can retry failed file deliveries without losing chargebacks.
Client if you need per client auth, quotas, or tracing.
A simple mental model is this. Chargebacks arrive one by one, but Mastercard consumes them in a few big envelopes each day.
POST /chargebacks [ creates a new chargeback request to submit. Include an idempotency key.]
POST /batches/generate only if you want a manual or admin trigger. Otherwise make it internal.
